svg.aria-label: How to write ಭ: 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 7 movements
svg.title: Writing ಭ
svg.desc: 7 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ಭ (kannada), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansKannada-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Gopala Krishna A, Kannada-alphabet-bha.gif, animation of Kannada consonant ಭ, 33 frames, 3.3 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 25 May 2016) <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kannada-alphabet-bha.gif>. Source note on variation: The CC BY-SA 4.0 animation writes ಭ in three pen-down runs: from the curled tip inside the head the pen loops up over the head clockwise, slants down to the left, rounds the left lobe and rises into the middle point, drops round the right lobe and climbs the right side, curving over at the top (frames 0–11); after a lift, the short top bar from left to right curling up into the hook (frames 14–17); after a second lift, the tail below the point, drawn downward (frames 20–21). Its body is ಬ's. The frames were read from a mirror copy (234×189, 33 frames); no listed size for the Commons file was available to compare it with, so only the slug and the frames were checked. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Kannada outline rather than copying the animation's handwritten proportions; in that outline the head's curled tip is a short wedge, where the path starts, and the right side runs up into the bar instead of curving over, so the climb ends at the bar. These runs stage the letter one part at a time; they are not a count of how often fluent writers lift the pen, and no native writers' pen data for Kannada was available. Omniglot (Lake, Salakhutdinov & Tenenbaum, Science 350:1332, 2015; https://github.com/brendenlake/omniglot, MIT licence) holds 20 drawings of ಭ, each by a different Amazon Mechanical Turk worker copying a printed exemplar online. They are non-native copyists, not native writers; where the same dataset can be set beside native writers' pen data (HP Labs India's Devanagari and Bangla sets), the copyists use more strokes than those writers, so their counts are read here only as a ceiling on native lifts, and only counts and shares are cited. Even under that ceiling, 55% of them (11 of 20) draw ಭ in two strokes; 30% (6 of 20) use the animation's three. Those counts say how many strokes, not where they break, so this learner path keeps every run's order, start and direction as a segment and joins the body to the bar, running back left along the bar before drawing it into the hook, so the pen lifts once, before the tail.
svg.text: How it is written — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 7 movements
Stroke order after Gopala Krishna A, Kannada-alphabet-bha.gif, animation of Kannada consonant ಭ, 33 frames, 3.3 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 25 May 2016)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
